compatibility: Deploy additive Gateway list/preview-resource support before the consuming web application when a rollout is separately authorized.
Old clients remain valid; existing collection detail and product/mobile interfaces are unchanged.
No schema migration or business-data mutation introduced by this phase. Inherited programme prerequisites remain.
Public summaries are no-store; preview resource stays private/no-store behind the existing store/token/expiry/draft checks. No cross-request private cache.
failureRecovery: Current Core grid reads are mandatory for rendering that grid: failure reaches the existing whole-page retry boundary rather than rendering false empty data. This does not prove optional-component isolation or full-store outage behavior.
Backend-only rollback while new web serves makes discovery unavailable by design. Coordinate backend/web rollback; do not hide contract failure with empty data.
Application rollback restores prior discovery behavior, including its known synthetic wrapper limitation; it is not a claim of launch acceptance. Saved store/draft/release documents are untouched.
readBudget: At most24 manual summaries per invocation, title/id order, fixed projected fields, no exact count or product/membership fanout.
No database sort-cost, maximum payload size or useful-page latency improvement has been measured.
Collection pagination and misleading persisted browse-every copy are open; no merchant data/copy was silently rewritten.
release: No merge/push/deploy, hosted cutover, real provider effects or shared DB writes were performed.
